items.text: A fork is one piece attacking two enemy pieces at once. Here the knight checks the king and hits the rook. The king must move, so the rook falls.

items.prompt: Tap every black piece the knight attacks.
items.explain: The knight on e5 hits the queen on d7, the rook on f7 and the pawn on g6. Knights jump, so nothing can block them.

items.prompt: Which move forks the king and the rook?
items.explain: Nc7+ checks the king and attacks the rook on a8 together. Nd6+ is check too, but it hits nothing else.

items.prompt: True or false: after Nf7+, the knight attacks both the king and the queen.
items.explain: From f7 the knight checks the king on h8 and attacks the queen on d8.
Nc7+ checks the king and hits the rook on a8. The king has to step away, and the knight takes the rook.

items.text: Knights fork best. A knight jumps in an L, reaches up to eight squares, and nothing can block it. Here one knight hits the queen and the rook.

items.prompt: Tap every black piece the knight attacks.
items.explain: From e6 the knight hits d8, f8, c5 and g5: four pieces from one square. A knight deep in enemy ground is a fork waiting to happen.

items.prompt: Which knight move forks the king and the queen?
items.explain: Nf7+ checks the king on h8 and attacks the queen on d6. The king must answer the check, then the queen falls.

items.prompt: True or false: after Nc7, the knight attacks both rooks.
items.explain: From c7 the knight reaches a8 and e8, but not f8. One rook attacked is a threat, not a fork.
Nf6+ checks the king and attacks the queen on d5. After the king moves, the knight takes the queen.
Nc7+ hits the king, the rook on a8 and the queen on a6 at once: a family fork. Whatever Black does, the queen falls.

items.text: Any piece can fork. A pawn fork hurts most: the cheapest piece on the board attacks two that are worth more. Here the pawn hits a knight and a bishop.

items.prompt: Tap every black piece the pawn attacks.
items.explain: A pawn attacks one square diagonally forward on each side: c6 and e6. The pawn on b6 is in front of nothing, so it's safe.

items.prompt: Which pawn move forks both knights?
items.explain: d4 attacks both knights at once, and neither knight can take it. b4 hits only one.

items.prompt: Tap every black piece the queen attacks.
items.explain: From d4 the queen reaches a7, d7, g4 and h8 along her lines. The pawn on h4 is safe behind the one on g4: queens can't jump.

items.prompt: True or false: after Qe4+, the queen attacks both the king and the rook.
items.explain: Qe4+ checks along the diagonal to h7 and hits the rook on a8 along the other. Black must answer the check, and the rook goes.
Qd5+ checks the king along one diagonal and attacks the rook on a8 along the other. After the king steps aside, the queen takes the rook.
